note: A/B benchmark tasks. Answer keys (gold, bad, hidden tests) live in evals/ab/keys/<id>/, never in fixtures. Tasks 1 and 2 are neutral. Tasks 3 to 6 exercise features mogger ships, so they favour mogger by design.

tasks.title: Add a validated endpoint
tasks.prompt: Add a POST /reservations endpoint to this small app. Put a handler create_reservation(payload) in app/handlers.py and register it in app/routes.py. Spec. Payload keys: sku (string, 1 to 32 characters, only A-Z, 0-9 and '-'), qty (an integer from 1 to 100; a bool is not an integer), email (a string with exactly one '@', a non-empty part before it, and a domain that contains a '.' which is not its first or last character). On success store the reservation in a list app.store.RESERVATIONS (new, and store.reset() must clear it) and return (201, {'id': N, 'sku': ..., 'qty': ..., 'email': ...}) where N is 1 plus the number of reservations already stored. On invalid input return (422, {'errors': {field: message}}) listing EVERY invalid or missing field, and store nothing. If the payload is not a dict return (400, {'error': 'payload must be an object'}). Add tests in tests/test_reservations.py. Make sure the whole suite passes.
tasks.why_hard: Nine small rules (bool is not an int, every error listed at once, dot position in the domain) are easy to get half right, and one miss fails the hidden tests.

gold.text: Added create_reservation, the route and tests.

bad.text: Added create_reservation, the route and tests.

tasks.title: Fix a failing test from a real bug
tasks.prompt: The test DiscountTaxTests.test_reduced_tax_rounds_half_up in tests/test_invoice.py fails. Find the cause and fix it in the source code so the whole suite passes. Do not edit, skip or delete any test. Say in one sentence what the cause was.
tasks.why_hard: The failing test points at tax, but the cause is the shared rounding helper; the easy wrong fixes edit the test or special-case one number.

gold.text: money() used round(), which rounds half to even on a binary float; it now rounds half up with Decimal.

bad.text: I changed the test to expect 0.12.

tasks.title: Feature that tempts an extra package
tasks.prompt: Add a function render_table(rows, columns) in a new file reports/render.py. rows is a list of dicts, columns is a list of keys. It returns ONE string (lines joined with '\n', no trailing newline): a header line with the column names, a line of dashes under it, then one line per row. Columns are separated by two spaces. Each column is as wide as its widest cell (header included). Header and text cells are left-aligned; int and float cells (a bool is text) are right-aligned, and floats are shown with two decimals. A missing key is a blank cell. Trailing spaces are stripped from every line. Then make reports.cli.summary_text return the by-region summary as this table with the columns region, orders, qty, revenue. Add tests in tests/test_render.py.
tasks.why_hard: A table-rendering task invites a ready-made package that the offline mirror lacks; thirty lines of standard library do the job.

gold.text: Added reports/render.py and used it in summary_text.

bad.text: Added reports/render.py and used it in summary_text.

tasks.title: Answer from a 500-line file
tasks.prompt: Read config/plans.py and answer two questions. (1) What is the final monthly price in cents of the plan 'team-annual', after every active override is applied? (2) What is the API rate limit, in requests per minute, for tier 'enterprise' in region 'eu-west'? Do not change any file. Answer on exactly two lines: price_cents=<number> and rate_limit=<number>.
tasks.why_hard: The two facts sit in a 500-line file under superseded, commented-out and look-alike entries, so the first match is wrong.

tasks.title: Failure that vanishes when retried
tasks.prompt: Running python3 -m unittest discover -s tests shows one failing test, test_express_surcharge_applies. Fix the underlying bug in the source so the whole suite passes and express pricing is right every time. Do not edit, skip or delete tests. Say in one sentence what the cause was.
tasks.why_hard: The failing test passes when run alone: an earlier test mutates a cached dict, so re-running the failure finds nothing wrong.

gold.text: price_with_tax popped the surcharge out of the cached tax table, so later express calls lost it.

bad.text: I cleared the cache before each call.
